feasibility_reasoning:
The one-line change is safe mechanically. src/lib/ssrCache.ts:65-72 is read only by l2Allowed (:192-195). No test or gate pins the list. The cached values are anonymous JSON row arrays fetched with the singleton anon client. Ads are projected after the read (ads/queries.ts:181). The random post-list is excluded (postListQuery.ts:444-448).

It breaks the claim that freshness matches today's L1. A post publish runs a selective purge: "/" is always in the list (documentCache.ts:324), and documentCache.server.ts:986-1004 deletes the document from L1 and L2. That purge does not bump the host version (ssrCacheL2.server.ts:28-30). No code invalidates builder:* keys; invalidateEdgeTtlCache is called only from menus and donations.

Today a cold isolate re-rendering "/" fetches the post lists fresh. With SC-2 it reads the colo-wide pre-publish snapshot instead: up to 60 s fresh, or up to 300 s stale and served immediately (ssrCache.ts:41-45, 371-374). It then stores a homepage without the new post: 180 s fresh, then 24 h of serving stale (documentCache.ts:47,57).

The fixture verification cannot run. In Node getColoCache() returns null (documentCacheL2.server.ts:92-100), so the mechanism can only be shown in a vitest with setEdgeTtlL2Adapter. The production check "db n<23" does not tell the cases apart, because n=23 already means a fully cold colo.
blocking_issues: Selective purge on post publish deletes '/' from document L2 but leaves builder:* snapshots in place (ssrCacheL2.server.ts:28-30; documentCache.server.ts:986-1004). With SC-2 the re-rendered homepage shows the pre-publish post lists from colo L2 and is stored for 180 s plus serve-stale. Needs a purge-aware guard: bump a per-host data version, or reject snapshots with at < purgedAt, whenever '/' is purged.

The verification plan is not runnable. The Node fixture has no colo cache (documentCacheL2.server.ts:92-100), and the production 'db n<23' check does not tell the cases apart (n=23 is a fully cold colo, where SC-2 does nothing).
effect_reasoning:
The claim "4 DB waves -> ~0" double-counts waves that are already in L2. trace-120.jsonl maps as follows:
- W1 settings, tokens and menus: already L2.
- W2 pages and W3 get_entity_content run inside public:home-page (public.ts:538): already L2.
- W3 get_post_refs runs inside trending_posts resolveAuthors (postViews.functions.ts:124): already L2.
- W4 (5x posts, builder:*) and the ad_placements leg in W2 are the new keys.
- W5 newsletter_settings is never cached (useNewsletterSettings.ts:191).

So a cold isolate in a warm colo pays about 1 DB wave before the shell today. SC-2 saves 1 RTT, 0.09-0.2 s. Bots wait for allReady, so they still pay W5 newsletter_settings.

The case is also rare. Document L2 serves STALE for 24 h (documentCache.ts:57), so a cold isolate in a warm colo usually returns HIT/STALE without rendering. Data snapshots live at most 300 s. SC-2 therefore fires only after a post publish deletes "/", after a degraded render, or for a sibling variant rendered within the last 5 min. A fully cold PSI colo has an empty data L2, and that is where degraded renders happen. On a warm colo the single remaining wave (~0.2 s) already fits inside HOME_SSR_BUDGET_MS=600 (homeSsrBudget.ts:15).

Score arithmetic (Lantern charges TTFB only to SI, per SC-F1):
- Desktop: about 1.8 perf points per second of TTFB ((94-96 minus 90-91) / 2.5 s). 0.15 s gives about 0.27 points.
- Mobile: SI grows about 0.66 ms per ms of TTFB. 0.1 s of SI at roughly 5 s SI is about 0.012 x 10% weight, about 0.1 points.
- Multiplied by P(case) of 10% or less, the expected value is about 0.01-0.03 points.
corrected_estimate: -0.09...-0.2 s MISS TTFB, only for the narrow class "cold isolate + '/' missing from colo document L2 + data snapshots < 300 s old". 0 s on fully cold colos and on HIT/STALE. Degraded renders do not drop materially. Expected PSI effect is about 0 points (<0.05 desktop, <0.02 mobile).
better_alternative: Only ship SC-2 together with a purge-aware guard: a selective purge of '/' must also invalidate builder:* snapshots (per-host data-version bump or a purgedAt marker). Wrapping newsletter_settings in edgeTtlCache with L2 removes the last W5 DB wave that bots wait for. For the score itself, raise the document HIT ratio in the colos PSI uses (cross-colo L3 snapshot or regional warmers, SC-F5); SC-2 will not move it.
